reference: Contract oracle: GNU Bash type/help builtin behavior, documented vi loadable behavior in vi.c and sol-vi.md, and POSIX vi command semantics (including A appending after the end of the current line). Expected output bytes are fixed from those contracts before candidate execution. No GNU vi CLI is guaranteed by the runner, so editor operations are contracts rather than fabricated parity comparisons.
coverage: Bash type -t identifies vi as a builtin.
Bash help exposes the vi usage and documented no-TTY key driver.
Ex line deletion and writing the resulting buffer to a relative fixture file.
No-TTY key driver insertion, Escape, and :wq save behavior, including POSIX A append-at-end semantics.
Counted G plus dd, including preservation of a missing final newline.
Visual character deletion followed by undo and redo.
Default refusal of a NUL-containing input file.
exclusions: No GNU vi executable is assumed. The named Nvim reference covers only the selected ordinary Unicode a/$a/A edits; all other editor expectations remain explicit contracts.
Interactive screen rendering, terminal input decoding, and terminal resize need a PTY driver and are deferred.
Macros, marks, named registers, substitute regex, syntax highlighting, plugins, and complex motions are documented as outside the shipped subset.

cases.purpose: Bash type -t must identify an enabled loadable as a builtin; this is the documented Bash type contract.
Bash help must expose the documented vi synopsis, POSIX-subset description, and no-TTY --keys form.
cases.script:
doc=$(help vi)
[[ $(type -t vi) == builtin ]] || exit 1
[[ $doc == *'Minimal modal vi editor (POSIX subset) for bash-os.'* ]] || exit 1
[[ $doc == *'vi [-b] --keys KEYFILE [PATH]'* ]] || exit 1
printf 'vi help metadata present\n'

cases.purpose: The documented ex address 2d deletes the second line; w saves exactly the remaining bytes to a relative path.
cases.script:
printf 'red\ngreen\nblue\n' > input
rc=0
vi -c '2d' -c 'w result' -c 'q!' input || rc=$?
[[ $rc -eq 0 ]] || exit 1
/usr/bin/python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; import sys; sys.stdout.buffer.write(Path('"'"'result'"'"').read_bytes())'

cases.purpose: POSIX vi defines A to append after the current line's last character; the no-TTY key driver must process A, Escape, and :wq and save the exact edited line.
cases.script:
printf 'Hello\n' > input
printf 'A, world!\033:wq\r' > keys
rc=0
vi --keys keys input || rc=$?
[[ $rc -eq 0 ]] || exit 1
/usr/bin/python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; import sys; sys.stdout.buffer.write(Path('"'"'input'"'"').read_bytes())'

cases.purpose: The documented [N]G motion and dd line delete remove line three while preserving the input's missing final newline in the saved result.
cases.script:
printf 'north\nsouth\nwest\neast' > input
printf '3Gdd:w result\r:q!\r' > keys
rc=0
vi --keys keys input || rc=$?
[[ $rc -eq 0 ]] || exit 1
/usr/bin/python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; import sys; sys.stdout.buffer.write(Path('"'"'result'"'"').read_bytes())'

cases.purpose: The documented visual x delete and u/Ctrl-R history commands must restore then reapply a characterwise selection before save.
cases.script:
printf 'alpha beta\n' > input
printf 'vllxu\022:w result\r:q!\r' > keys
rc=0
vi --keys keys input || rc=$?
[[ $rc -eq 0 ]] || exit 1
/usr/bin/python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; import sys; sys.stdout.buffer.write(Path('"'"'result'"'"').read_bytes())'

cases.purpose: Without -b, the documented binary-content tripwire must reject a relative input containing NUL with failure and a diagnostic.
cases.script:
printf 'a\0b\n' > input
: > keys
rc=0
vi --keys keys input || rc=$?
[[ $rc -eq 1 ]] || exit 1
printf 'NUL input refused\n'

cases.purpose: Track interactive normal/insert/command-mode screen behavior and saves when the editor owns a real terminal.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM with a controlled PTY and terminal settings plus an independent POSIX vi reference. The supplied runner starts fixtures with stdin disconnected to /dev/null and has no PTY facility, so no interactive operation was executed. A future test must use only relative fixture files and compare final bytes and bounded screen behavior inside that VM.

cases.purpose: Track terminal arrow-key decoding and viewport behavior after a deterministic window resize.
cases.reason: Requires a disposable VM PTY driver that can set TERM/terminfo and resize the terminal to fixed dimensions, along with an independent vi reference. The current runner cannot allocate or resize a PTY. Future fixtures must use scripted key bytes and relative files only; this behavior was not run or claimed as passed.

cases.purpose: Ex deletion then q! leaves the original bytes unchanged.
cases.script: printf 'one\ntwo\n' > input; vi -c '1d' -c 'q!' input; cat input

cases.purpose: Bounded no-TTY insertion uses i, Escape and :wq.
cases.script: : > input; printf 'iabc\033:wq\r' > keys; vi --keys keys input; cat input

cases.purpose: Documented a appends after the complete current UTF-8 character, preserving the following character and newline. Inserting ASCII after e-acute must not split its two-byte encoding.
cases.script:
printf 'éZ\n' > input
printf 'a!\033:wq\r' > keys
vi --keys keys input
IFS= read -r line < input
printf '%s\n' "$line"

cases.purpose: Documented $a appends after a final multibyte character, and ordinary undo/redo preserves the complete edited Unicode bytes before :wq.
cases.script:
printf 'café\n' > input
printf '$a!\033u\022:wq\r' > keys
vi --keys keys input
IFS= read -r line < input
printf '%s\n' "$line"

cases.purpose: Compare the documented a and $a edits on valid UTF-8 with independent Nvim in silent headless mode, using private 0600 files and no terminal. This is selected Nvim editing parity, not GNU/full vi conformance.
cases.script:
printf 'éZ\n' > middle
printf 'café\n' > ending
chmod 600 middle ending
printf 'a!\033:wq\r' > middle.keys
printf '$a!\033:wq\r' > ending.keys
if [[ $(type -t vi) == builtin ]]; then
 vi --keys middle.keys middle
 vi --keys ending.keys ending
else
 nvim --headless -u NONE -i NONE -n -es middle -c $'normal! a!\033' -c wq
 nvim --headless -u NONE -i NONE -n -es ending -c $'normal! $a!\033' -c wq
fi
IFS= read -r first < middle
IFS= read -r second < ending
printf '%s\n%s\n' "$first" "$second"

cases.purpose: Compare end-of-line A on ASCII, Unicode and an empty line, and repeating the append on a second line with dot, against independent headless Nvim using private files. Counted A and interactive rendering remain outside this case. Both drivers explicitly start at the first line because silent Nvim otherwise starts at the last line.
cases.script:
printf 'éZ\nlast\n' > lines
printf '\n' > empty
chmod 600 lines empty
printf '1G0A!\033j0.\033:wq\r' > lines.keys
printf 'Aword\033:wq\r' > empty.keys
if [[ $(type -t vi) == builtin ]]; then
 vi --keys lines.keys lines
 vi --keys empty.keys empty
else
 nvim --headless -u NONE -i NONE -n -es lines -c $'normal! 1G0A!\033j0.' -c wq
 nvim --headless -u NONE -i NONE -n -es empty -c $'normal! Aword\033' -c wq
fi
cat lines empty
